title: He touched dirt… and called it healing.
paragraphs:
He touched dirt… and called it healing.
He didn’t repeat Himself—and that’s what unsettles us.

You expected a formula.
A method.
A predictable move of God you could memorize.

But what if the reason your miracle hasn’t happened…
is because you’re trying to control the way Jesus moves?

You prayed like them.
You fasted like them.
You declared the same words.

Still broken.
Still bleeding.
Still unanswered.
And deep down… shame starts whispering:
“Maybe God moves for others… but not for you.”

We don’t just want healing.
We want control disguised as faith.
We want God to follow our script.
He refuses to be reduced to a method.

Jesus spits on the ground.
Makes mud.
Presses it into his eyes.
Another man is dying miles away.

No touch.
No mud.
No physical presence.
“Go; let it be done for you as you have believed.” — Matthew 8:13
And the servant is healed… at that very moment.

Twelve years bleeding.
Twelve years hiding.
Twelve years of quiet shame.

She pushes through the crowd—
reaches—
touches the edge of His garment.
“Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace.” — Luke 8:48

Different methods.
Different moments.
Different encounters.
Why would Jesus heal in so many different ways?
Why not just do it once… and repeat the formula?
Because the goal was never the method.
You’re not a copy of someone else’s testimony.
You’re not a duplicated miracle waiting for a repeated script.
You are a person Jesus wants to meet personally.
And here’s where it cuts deep—
Sometimes your delay is not denial.

Invitation to stop performing.
Invitation to stop comparing.
Invitation to stop striving.
“Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” — Hebrews 13:8

His power doesn’t change.
His methods do.
Because He’s not trying to mass-produce miracles.
Some scholars interpret these varied healings as intentional demonstrations that Jesus is not bound by ritual, environment, or distance—His authority is absolute, personal, and sovereign.
Your healing will not look like theirs.
Because your story is not theirs.
The greatest healing Jesus ever gave…

Was not blind eyes.
Not restored skin.
Not physical breakthrough.
It was the healing of sin.
Let’s talk about the deeper wound.
The one behind the smiles, the church attendance, the “I’m okay.”

The secret sin.
The quiet compromise.
The guilt you carry when no one’s watching.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

That includes you.
That includes me.
No amount of good works, rituals, or religious patterns can fix it.
You cannot “method” your way out of sin.
He didn’t spit on dirt this time.
He didn’t just speak from a distance.
“By His wounds we are healed.” — Isaiah 53:5
On that cross, Jesus carried your sin.

Your shame.
Your hidden battles.
Your failures.
And He didn’t heal you from a distance.

You are more sinful than you want to admit…
but more loved than you can imagine.
Salvation is not found in a method.
It is found in a Man.
“Repent, therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.” — Acts 3:19
Returning to the One who heals differently…

Are you chasing a method…
or are you seeking Jesus?
Because the same Jesus who touched the leper…
The same Jesus who responded to a desperate woman…
is listening to your silent cry.
The same Jesus who healed with a word…
can speak life into your situation.
And He’s not offering you a technique.
